resources.string: Nothing matches in the states that are switched on. The chips show where the matches are.
Nothing is in the states that are switched on.
Nagios will be told: %1$s to %2$s (its clock is %3$s).
The end has to be after the start, and still to come.

Nothing has been sent. This Nagios shows the time now as “%1$s”. Today the day and the month are the same number, so Nagwatch cannot tell which order this server uses, and a guess could put the downtime on the wrong day. Any other date in the Nagios web interface will show you.
Downtime scheduled, for the window asked for.
Not sent. Nagwatch needs to know how this Nagios writes dates.
Nagios scheduled a different window from the one asked for. Asked: %1$s to %2$s. Scheduled: %3$s to %4$s.

This Nagios is on your local network. Android asks before an app may reach devices there, and calls the permission “Nearby devices”. Nagwatch only talks to the address you entered; it does not search for or scan other devices.\n\nIf you say no, Nagwatch still tries, which works when you reach Nagios over a VPN.
Problems on one Nagios, from a single number up to a list.
No profile. Tap to choose one.

Choose the Nagios this widget shows. Nagwatch will check it in the background, at the interval set in its profile, for as long as the widget is on your home screen. That happens even with notifications off; it does not turn them on. The widget shows host and service names on your home screen.
There are no profiles yet. Add one in Nagwatch, then place the widget again.

How much of your wallpaper shows through, from 0% (all of it) to 100% (none). The background is washed with the colour of the worst problem. A widget that is out of date is never fainter than 60%, so you can still tell.

How often Nagwatch checks this Nagios while the app is closed. It applies when this profile has notifications on or a widget on the home screen; otherwise nothing is checked in the background. Android decides exactly when, so allow for it running late.
Nagwatch checks this Nagios in the background and tells you when something new is wrong. Expect news to be up to the interval above late, and later while the phone is idle.
Android is not letting Nagwatch show notifications, so this stays off.
Leaves out problems that are acknowledged or in scheduled downtime.
Tell me when this Nagios can’t be reached
After three checks in a row get no answer. Worth turning off for a Nagios you can only reach at home. A rejected password is always reported.
Nagwatch can check %1$s in the background about every 15 minutes and tell you when something new is wrong.\n\nYou can change this at any time in the profile’s settings.
Android is not letting Nagwatch show notifications. This Nagios is still checked in the background, but you will not be told what it finds.
Acknowledged. It is with the handled problems now.
What an acknowledgement says when you make one from a list or a notification, without the form. Everyone who uses this Nagios will see it. Leave empty for “Acknowledged from Nagwatch”.

Android keeps the sound, importance and vibration for each kind of notification: down and critical, warning, unknown, recovered, can’t reach Nagios and summaries. Android lists them under “Other”. What you set there applies to every profile.
Unlock the phone to do this. Nothing was sent.
Checked again. The next background check will show what it found.
Nagios accepted this, but it has not taken effect yet. Open to see where it stands.
Nagios has not answered the last few checks. You will not hear about new problems until it does.
Its certificate is not being accepted, so nothing is being checked.
Something other than Nagios is answering at its address. A sign-in page on this network, perhaps.
Nagios is answering with an error, so nothing is being checked.
Android may be blocking Nagwatch from your local network. Open Nagwatch to allow it.
Nagios rejected the username or password. Nothing is being checked until that is put right in the profile.
Cloudflare Access rejected the token. Nothing is being checked until that is put right in the profile.
Nagios will not let this user see status. Nothing is being checked.
The saved password can no longer be read on this phone. Enter it again in the profile.
The profile’s address cannot be used as it is. Open the profile to put it right.
This Nagios user is read-only, so actions are unavailable.
Ends when the state next changes, so a problem that gets worse notifies again.
A sticky acknowledgement stays until this recovers, even if it gets worse first. Nobody is notified in that time.
Tell the contacts it was acknowledged
Keep the comment after the acknowledgement ends
Nagios will treat this as an unhandled problem again and may notify its contacts.
Nagios accepted it. Waiting to see it take effect…
Nagios accepted this, but it has not taken effect yet. It may still: pull down to look again.
This may or may not have reached Nagios. Look at what it shows now before trying again.
This may or may not have reached Nagios. Look at what it shows now before trying again. %1$s
Nagios refused: this user is read-only.
Nagios refused: this user may not do that here, or the host or service no longer exists.
Nagios refused this and did not say why.
Nagios is not accepting commands: external commands are switched off on the server.
Nagios could not record the command. Nothing was changed. This is a fault on the server.
Nagios takes no commands while its own authentication is switched off.
The last refresh failed, so this may be out of date. %1$s
This is %1$s old. Pull down to refresh.
No unhandled problems. Everything left is acknowledged or in downtime.
details unavailable: Nagios could not read this one

plurals.name: problems_banner_degraded
plurals.item: Nagios could not provide the details of %1$d item (a server error on its side). It is listed with its state only.
Nagios could not provide the details of %1$d items (a server error on its side). They are listed with their state only.

resources.string: A symbol at the start of each notification, in case your phone does not colour the icon. It applies to every profile, from the next notification.
A circle in the state\u2019s colour beside each notification. Where your phone draws the app\u2019s own icon there, this replaces it. It applies from the next notification.
A profile is a connection to one Nagios instance. Add one to get started.
This URL is not encrypted. Your username and password are sent in a form anyone on the network path can read. Only use it on a network you trust.
Allow unencrypted HTTP for this profile
Optional. A service token, for a Nagios behind Cloudflare Access. Requires an https URL.
Optional. Extra headers for other proxies. Values are stored encrypted, like passwords.
Nagwatch is tested on Nagios 4.5. Older versions are expected to work, but have not been tried: if comments or downtimes are missing, that is why.
This Nagios user is read-only. Nagwatch will show everything, but cannot acknowledge, comment or recheck with it.
The saved credentials for this profile can no longer be read. This happens after restoring a device. Enter them again and save.
“%1$s” and its saved credentials will be removed from this device.
That is not a valid http or https URL.
This is an unencrypted http URL. Turn on “Allow unencrypted HTTP” to use it, or use https.
Cloudflare Access credentials are never sent over unencrypted http. Use an https URL, or remove them.
Cloudflare Access needs both a client ID and a client secret.
A header name may only contain letters, digits and - _ . and similar symbols.
That header is set by Nagwatch from the fields above and cannot be overridden.
The graph path must be a path on this Nagios server, like /nagiosgraph/cgi-bin/. It cannot be a full URL or name another server.
Graph of %1$s over the last %2$s, drawn by nagiosgraph. Tap for full screen.
Graph of %1$s over the last %2$s, drawn by nagiosgraph. Pinch to zoom, double-tap to reset.
There is no graph for this period.
The graph could not be fetched just now.
A service\u2019s history as nagiosgraph draws it, where the server has nagiosgraph and the service has performance data. Where it has not, nothing is shown.
Leave empty if nagiosgraph is in the same cgi-bin as Nagios. Otherwise its path on this server, like /nagiosgraph/cgi-bin/
Cloudflare Access rejected the request. Check the client ID and secret, and that the service token is allowed by the Access policy and has not expired.
Nagios rejected the username or password.
The server refused access for this user.
The server\'s certificate is not trusted: %1$s. If your Nagios uses a private certificate authority, install its certificate in Android Settings under Security.
The server name could not be found. Check the URL and your network connection.
Nothing is accepting connections at that address. Check the URL and port, and that you are on the right network.
The server did not answer in time.

The server did not answer. Android may be blocking Nagwatch from your local network: it needs the “Nearby devices” permission to reach an address there. If this Nagios is not on your network at the moment, check that it is running instead.
Something answered, but it is not Nagios. Check the URL; it should be the address of the Nagios web interface.
This profile uses unencrypted http, which is not enabled for it.
Cloudflare Access credentials are never sent over unencrypted http.
The server redirected to %1$s. Use that address as the URL instead.
The server sent more data than Nagwatch will accept.
